text:
alex: Hey team — working on a docs PR for SDK retention language. Need SOC2-friendly sample sentences for short vs long retention and a tiny migration blurb for customers. Thoughts?

maria: 👍 can you paste where this will live? is it under /security/audit-logs or the SDK reference?

alex: It'll be a new subsection under /docs/security/audit-logs.md and we also want a snippet in the SDK guides (python + curl) showing how to request export retention.
dave: For wording I usually keep it: 'We retain audit logs for X days to meet compliance obligations. Customers may configure retention up to Y days via the Console or API.' short and factual.

jen: +1. Add a sentence about data minimization: 'Only the metadata necessary for auditing (request id, timestamp, actor) is retained; sensitive payloads are redacted or excluded from audit exports unless explicitly requested.'

samira: Legal note: avoid promising specific days unless backed by policy. Use ranges and opt-in language. E.g., 'Default retention is 90 days; customers can request extended retention up to 365 days under a contractual agreement.' If a hard number exists due to product defaults, call it 'default'.

alex: Good point. So draft: 'Default retention: 90 days. Extended retention can be provisioned by request and is subject to contract and applicable regulatory constraints.' Works?

maria: Works. Also include short migration blurb: 'When migrating from legacy audit exports, customers should re-ingest retained events into the new system. Use the export API with the following minimal curl example.'

alex: Adding snippets — please sanity-check:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit-exports" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"range": {"from": "2024-01-01","to":"2024-03-31"}, "redact": true}'
```

dave: Suggest adding note: `redact: true` will remove payloads that match sensitive schemas; timestamps and request ids remain.

jen: For SDK sample (python):
```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
client.create_export(from_date="2024-01-01", to_date="2024-03-31", redact=True)
```

samira: Add compliance-friendly phrasing: 'Exports are provisioned for a limited time. Customers who need long-term archival should use their own storage integrations or request a dedicated retention arrangement.'

alex: Ok I'll incorporate. One more: do we need to mention encryption/rotation here or link out to key-management page?

maria: Link out to the KMS page. Don't duplicate. Add a line: 'Exports are encrypted in transit and at rest; see Key Management for details.' with link.

alex: Draft PR ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1423 — includes updated audit-logs.md, SDK snippets, and a short migration checklist. Would love a quick review.

docs-bot: PR opened by alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1423 (labels: docs, compliance)

dave: quick pass LGTM for wording. Left one comment about 'sensitive schemas' examples — maybe list examples (PII, auth tokens).

jen: I'll add a short example list and a small note on redaction heuristics.

samira: From legal side this is good. Please ensure the 'extended retention' workflow routes to sales/contracting.

alex: Thanks — will add routing note and resolve comments. Planning to merge tomorrow after docs CI. :thumbsup:

maria: Awesome, ping if you want me to edit for tone before merge.

alex: Will do. Thank you!
